name: Hawaii

events.title: Statehood
events.text: Hawaii became the 50th state on August 21, 1959. Congress gave it 1 seat in the House until the next apportionment.

events.title: 1960 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1960 census, Hawaii's House delegation grew from 1 to 2 seats.

events.title: Statewide (general ticket) elections
events.text: In the 88th through 91st Congresses (1963–1971), Hawaii elected all of its representatives statewide on a general ticket instead of by district.

events.title: Two members elected statewide
events.text: When Hawaii gained a second seat after the 1960 census, it elected both members statewide. The 1967 federal law requiring single-member districts let Hawaii keep at-large elections for a time.

events.title: Reapportionment Commission draws the lines
events.text: Since 1968, a nine-member Reapportionment Commission has drawn Hawaii's congressional and state legislative districts. Legislative leaders each pick two members, and those eight choose a ninth; the state Supreme Court picks one if they cannot agree.

events.title: Switch from at-large to two districts
events.text: Hawaii was divided into two geographic congressional districts in 1970, ending statewide elections for its two House seats. The 1967 federal district law had let Hawaii keep at-large elections temporarily.

events.title: 1970 census apportionment
events.text: After the 1970 census, Hawaii kept 2 seats in the House. Because districts must have nearly equal populations, the map was redrawn with the new census counts.

compactnessNote: Polsby-Popper compactness (4π × area ÷ perimeter²) measured on the projected district shapes. It describes shape only: coastlines, rivers and county lines lower it too, so a low score is not evidence of intent. "Irregular" marks the least compact 5% of district shapes in each census era nationally.

c092.text: Hawaii's district lines were redrawn between censuses, first used in the 1970 election. The reason has not been researched yet.

c098.text: New map drawn after the 1980 census, which left Hawaii with 2 seats. It was first used in the 1982 election.

c099.text: Not a new map: the historical boundary records show only slight differences in 2 districts from the previous Congress, and no statewide redistricting is recorded for this election.

c103.text: New map drawn after the 1990 census, which left Hawaii with 2 seats. It was first used in the 1992 election.
